[runbook draft 2026-11-13 section 1 of 4]
This runbook is blocked on the final C2 consumer and old-tool safety reports.
Do not execute its live steps tonight.

The owner approved the conditional basicly release and development-only switch on 2026-11-13.
Basicly, handily and terminal keep their current trackers.
The owner selected a private backlog-vault and no private id map.
Old external references to reminted event ids cannot use a migration map after this switch.
Normal vault reads and writes need no map.

Before release or a live switch step, stop and ask the owner on any refusal, failed check or differing count.
Other work fixes the cause without weakening a gate.

The retained part 1 rehearsal measured these values before the planned consumer writes.
Run this command from `basicly.worktrees/codex-vault-cut-d` with the private fixture alias supplied through the environment.

```sh
python3 .scripts/rehearse_vault_migration.py --source-repo ../.. --out ../../.orchestrator/codex-1-cut-d --part part1
```

| Item | Measured value |
| --- | --- |

| Source events | 491 |
| Carried events | 491 |
| Reminted events | 45 |
| View and export events | 504 |
| Current reviews | 2 |
| Current confirmations | 4 |
| Closed records | 19 |

The export includes derived holder events.

The standalone preview and import digests agreed.
The saved copy stays frozen while the live workspace ledger can grow.

The copied consumer control has one record and three source events.
Its marker and source ledger bytes remained unchanged during import.
The scratch root is `.orchestrator/codex-1-cut-d` relative to the workspace.
The vault is `vault-0.git` there.
Keep these folders until the owner approves their removal.

The proposed release version is `0.46.0` because the release adds migration capabilities.
This version is a planning choice, not a published release.
Cut B is pushed at `5f876ad7` with green required main CI and passing destination verification.
The D helper is pushed separately at `ba5e9d18` and is not on main.

1. Wait for cut B and cut C2 on main with green required CI.
   Run the final development-copy rehearsal from that main commit.
   Include record identities, event accounting, process evidence, template checks and the old beads comparison.
   Obtain codex-2's final lifecycle and legacy-consumer reports from the same landed source.
   Record the exact commits, commands, digests and counts here.
   Replace this draft's provisional values before showing the final runbook to the owner.

2. Prepare the release in its own tracked record and lane.
   Use the proposed version only after all required source and consumer checks pass.
   Add the release summary before the release command assembles its commit and tag.
   Land the notes through the normal lock and hooks.
   Wait for green required main CI.
   Use the primary basicly checkout for the release command, as its guard requires.
   The release commit refers to the completed rehearsal record.

   ```sh
   uv run basicly release 0.46.0 --issue basicly-gtb19bg.43.33 --dry-run
   uv run basicly release 0.46.0 --issue basicly-gtb19bg.43.33
   git push origin main
   git push origin v0.46.0
   ```

   Run each command separately and inspect its result before the next command.
   Keep the main lock through the main push and release it immediately afterward.
   Confirm the tag workflow and published release before installing the release in development.
   A release failure requires the owner before any further release action.

[runbook draft 2026-11-13 section 2 of 4]
3. Upgrade the shared WSL engine, then install its kit in development only.
   The Orchestrator selected this order because daily commands use the global engine.
   Other repositories keep their installed kits and local trackers.
   Their `basicly check` version-skew result still needs the candidate comparison report.
   Tracker commands and commit hooks must pass that comparison before this step.
   The Windows global tool stays unchanged.
   The released old kit and engine must refuse safely or read correctly against the switched scratch repository.
   A silent local write or changed vault configuration blocks the live switch.

   From the workspace, first record the clean base commit and acquire its coordination lock.
   The workspace installation task must be filed, reviewed and claimed before managed-file writes.

   ```sh
   development_before_vault=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
   uv tool install --python '>=3.14' --force https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/releases/download/v0.46.0/basicly-0.46.0-py3-none-any.whl
   basicly --version
   basicly install --dry-run
   basicly install
   basicly check
   basicly hooks-check
   ```

   Expected version is `0.46.0`.
   Inspect the dry-run paths before installation.
   Do not use `--force` on `basicly install` or overwrite scaffolds.
   Save the exact workspace installation commit for recovery.
   The final staging and commit commands require the dry-run path list and workspace task id.
   The wheel install syntax is verified against `uv 0.13.7` help and the vendor's tool guide.
   Source: <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/tools/>.
   Stop on any refusal or failed check.
   Do not install another consumer under this approval.

   After an owner decision to roll back the engine, use the old wheel explicitly.

   ```sh
   uv tool install --python '>=3.14' --force https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/releases/download/v0.45.0/basicly-0.45.0-py3-none-any.whl
   ```

   Revert the recorded workspace installation commit through normal hooks before using its old kit again.
   Do not discard uncommitted work.

4. Freeze development writes through agent mail and acquire `development-main`.
   Confirm that no other writer will change the source during import and switch validation.
   Record the frozen source commit, file digests, record ids and event counts.
   Keep `.basicly/ledger` and `.beads` intact.
   Keep the source snapshot outside the vault and never publish its private contents.

5. Refresh visibility immediately before the first vault publication.
   Run these commands from the workspace.

   ```sh
   gh repo view niksavis/development --json nameWithOwner,visibility
   gh repo view niksavis/backlog-vault --json nameWithOwner,visibility
   git ls-remote https://github.com/niksavis/backlog-vault.git
   ```

   Both visibility results must be readable.
   The destination must report `PRIVATE`.
   The destination must meet the initializer's empty-repository requirement.
   An unreadable result, a public destination or unexpected refs stops the procedure.
   Do not interpret an empty response from a failed command as an empty repository.

[runbook draft 2026-11-13 section 3 of 4]
6. Initialize the private vault without switching development configuration.
   Omit `--prefix`, because the initializer writes project configuration only when that flag is present.
   Confirm this behavior against the landed C2 implementation and its consumer proof.

   ```sh
   python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py vault-init --vault https://github.com/niksavis/backlog-vault.git
   python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py vault-init --vault https://github.com/niksavis/backlog-vault.git --yes
   ```

   The first command previews genesis and must not publish or write project configuration.
   Inspect each result before proceeding.
   The second command publishes genesis and must leave `.basicly-tracker.toml` absent.
   Unexpected existing data stops the procedure.

7. Preview and import the frozen development ledger with the installed standalone kit.
   Use the same source and redaction rules as the final rehearsal.
   Imported history keeps the human holder text already present in the old ledger.
   Standard secret and machine-path redaction remains enabled.
   The rehearsal counted nine source events carrying that human holder, without printing the value.
   New human claims use the privately chosen alias through Git holder configuration.
   Agent identities remain distinct.
   If you want the alias to replace your name in imported history too, say so before this step.
   That choice needs an alias-history implementation and matching rehearsal before publication.

   ```sh
   python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate .basicly/ledger --to-vault --preview
   python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate .basicly/ledger --to-vault --vault https://github.com/niksavis/backlog-vault.git --no-map-kept
   ```

   Compare the actual source counts, reminted count and canonical digest with the frozen rehearsal.
   The import checks integrity and accounting before publication.
   Any differing count or digest stops the procedure.
   Do not repeat a refused one-time import.

8. Export the private vault into a new empty local folder before changing project configuration.
   Use a new empty export folder and never reuse a failed export destination.

   ```sh
   python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate .orchestrator/codex-1-live-check/export --from-vault --vault https://github.com/niksavis/backlog-vault.git --prefix dev
   python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py fsck .orchestrator/codex-1-live-check/export
   ```

   Verify record ids, statuses, process evidence, template identity and source event accounting.
   Compare the ready set with the frozen source using the rehearsal's validated comparison command.
   Stop on any failed comparison before writing project configuration.

[runbook draft 2026-11-13 section 4 of 4]
9. Write `.basicly-tracker.toml` only after the independent export passes.
   Create configuration exclusively, so an existing file refuses instead of being overwritten.

   ```sh
   python3 - <<'PY'
   from pathlib import Path
   with Path('.basicly-tracker.toml').open('x', encoding='utf-8') as target:
       target.write('vault = "https://github.com/niksavis/backlog-vault.git"\nprefix = "dev"\n')
   PY
   basicly tracker ready
   basicly tracker show dev-6pb60 --view current
   ```
   Configure the private human holder only through Git configuration when needed.
   Agents retain their own holder identities.
   Run the installed legacy-command aliases and supported vault commands from development.
   Verify that reads use the vault view and that supported writes leave the frozen local ledger unchanged.
   C2 intends ordinary ledger-form writes to queue vault events without local ledger writes.
   Compatible `claim` and `unassign` aliases use native vault ownership and its exit codes.
   `assign`, `resolve`, `acknowledge-loss` and `delete` refuse with a remedy.
   `claim --to`, `claim --take` and `unassign --by` also refuse.
   These behaviors need the final consumer and old-tool reports before live execution.
   Commit only the intended workspace configuration and installed release projections through normal hooks.
   Read mail before pushing and release `development-main` after the push.

10. Preserve recovery state after the switch.
    Before configuration changes, a failed import leaves development on its intact local ledger.
    Do not delete a partially initialized or imported vault.
    After configuration changes but before new vault writes, stop for the owner before reverting the configuration.
    After new vault writes, the frozen old ledger is stale.
    Drain the queue and export the full current canonical view before considering a return to local storage.
    If export or integrity checks fail, preserve both stores and ask the owner.
    Never point development back to the stale ledger silently.

Before execution, add C2's landed commit and final proof results, including old-tool safety and version skew.
Also add the live frozen snapshot identity, workspace task id, exact staging commands and recovery commit ids.

Its scratch consumer writes belong only to the rehearsal and must never be copied to the live source.
